exposure: spinal anaesthesia (SA) technique (L7-S1 vs L5-6/L6-7 interspaces for injection)
isobaric solution of bupivacaine and morphine dosage
outcome: incidence of hypotension (MAP <60 mmHg for ≥5 mins)
cohort: The study included 58 cats of American Society of Anaesthesiologists physical status I, II and III, who received combined general and spinal anaesthesia for various surgical procedures between 2012 and 2016.
finding: Spinal anaesthesia performed at the L5-6/L6-7 interspaces in cats resulted in a low procedural failure rate and low postoperative complications, although hypotension and bradycardia were identified as the most common side effects.
